description:
I'm a Toronto-based artist, music producer, and creative technologist with over 15 years of experience in creative projects.>  Python, data visualization, NASA APIs, sonification, web development, and interactive design.

My goal is to build a creative, functional prototype that turns scientific data into something people can hear, see, and explore. All skill levels and creative perspectives are welcome!
summary:
Melody Earth is an interactive web experience that turns NASA environmental data into a personal 30-second piano composition. A birth date, place and local time define the starting point for exploring Earth data and the sky. Transparent artistic rules translate scientific measurements into musical choices, allowing the same inputs to produce the same piece.

The project offers a creative way to engage with NASA data through listening and personal curiosity. It brings together music, Earth science and an interactive interface, inviting people to explore a connection between their own arrival and the planet. The music is an artistic interpretation of data, rather than a scientific reconstruction of sound at birth.
details:
Melody Earth is a browser-based musical experience developed by INFR Lab. Users enter a birth place, date and local time, then request a 30-second piano composition shaped by environmental data and the sky. The interface also offers an example for visitors to explore. The same inputs produce the same piece.

The project uses transparent artistic rules to translate data into musical decisions. Its goal is to encourage curiosity about Earth science through a personal listening experience. The resulting music is an artistic interpretation, not a claim that environmental measurements determine personality or that it recreates the actual sounds of a historical moment.

The prototype combines a web interface, NASA data lookups and generative piano music. NASA POWER is the environmental data resource identified for the project, and NASA Blue Marble imagery provides the visual Earth reference. The interface explains that online NASA lookups receive the selected date, coordinates and birth time, while the entered name remains in the page.

AI tools assisted research, coding, debugging, visual development and preparation of project materials. Scientific data and artistic mapping are distinct: measurements provide inputs, while musical rules are creative choices.
